title: Portugal Joins the Artemis Accords
text: Portugal became the 60th signatory to the Artemis Accords in January 2026. Helena Canhão, Portugal's Secretary of State for Science and Innovation, signed the accords on behalf of the country on 11 January. A ceremony in Lisbon was attended by John J. Arrigo, the United States Ambassador to Portugal, and Hugo Costa, executive director of the Portuguese Space Agency. The event coincided with a semi-annual meeting on cooperation between the United States and Portugal. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman welcomed Portugal as the newest signatory. Arrigo called Portugal's decision a meaningful step forward for responsible space exploration. Costa said that 2026 is the year humans return to the Moon, which will mark the beginning of a new era of space exploration, recalling Portuguese explorers such as Magellan.

questions.q: Who was the commander of NASA's Artemis II crewed mission?
questions.explanation: Reid Wiseman commanded Artemis II, which launched in April 2026. The other three names are Apollo-era astronauts who did not fly on Artemis II.

questions.q: Which of the following countries was NOT among the original signatories of the Artemis Accords?
questions.explanation: The original signatories were Australia, Canada, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, the UAE, the UK and the US. France was not among them.

list1: I. Year in which the Artemis Accords were launched
II. Year of the Outer Space Treaty on which the Accords' principles are grounded
III. Number of original signatories of the Artemis Accords
IV. Number of principles in the Artemis Accords
questions.explanation: The Accords were launched in 2020 (B) by eight original signatories (C). They set out ten principles (D) and are grounded in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty (A).

questions.assertion: The Artemis Accords are a legally binding treaty that the UN Security Council enforces against any signatory that breaks them.
questions.reason: The Artemis Accords are non-binding and provide no formal means of enforcement.
questions.explanation: Assertion is false: the Accords are not a binding treaty and the UN Security Council does not enforce them. Reason is true: the Accords are non-binding and have no formal enforcement mechanism, unlike the Outer Space Treaty.

statements: 1. The Artemis II mission lifted off on 1 April 2026.
2. Artemis II was a crewed flight around the Moon that did not land on it.
3. Artemis II landed astronauts on the lunar surface.
4. Artemis II launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Artemis II was a flyby without landing, and statement 4 is false because the launch was from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Two statements are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'.

statements: I. The North Atlantic Treaty was signed on 4 April 1949.
II. The North Atlantic Treaty entered into force on 1 January 1950.
III. Portugal was one of the original signatories of the North Atlantic Treaty.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are true. The treaty was signed on 4 April 1949 and Portugal was an original signatory. Statement II is false because the treaty entered into force on 24 August 1949.
